title: Choose EventPass’s new visual world
question: The dashboard can behave like a live production instrument, a disciplined run sheet, or one of two stronger outside systems. Choose the world to carry through the dashboard and administration experience.

options.label: Broadcast Rundown
options.thesis: EventPass becomes a calm live-production desk where every event, cue, and exception has a clear place in the running order.
options.viewport: A slim event rail frames one dominant live-event rundown: readiness, arrivals, communications, and the next operator actions move down a shared time axis.
options.risk: Can feel overly technical if routine planning screens inherit too much control-room density.

raised.raise: Color is confined to narrow status edges so the information field stays calm.
Motion always reveals cause and direction: updates travel toward the row they changed.
A strict density ladder distinguishes glanceable status from drill-down detail.
Every interactive state gains an unmistakable resting, armed, and active position.

options.label: The Run of Show
options.lineage: stage-management run sheets and cue books
options.thesis: The product becomes the operator’s beautifully typeset run of show: one authoritative sequence with annotations, owners, and live marks.
options.viewport: Today’s event opens as a spacious operational sheet with a timeline spine, readiness blocks, and a concise margin for alerts and responsibilities.
options.risk: It is the most familiar event-operations metaphor and can skew editorial if the live controls lose presence.

options.label: Concourse Board
options.thesis: Every active event becomes a departure row: time, venue, capacity, readiness, and exceptions resolve in one shared field.
options.viewport: A full-width operations board ranks live and upcoming events by time, with one expanded row exposing arrivals, delivery health, and immediate actions.
options.case: Strong operator recognition and excellent scanability; it loses flexibility when dense forms and permission administration need quieter composition.
options.risk: The fixed-cell grammar can become visually loud across long forms.

options.label: Operations Annual
options.thesis: Event operations read as a precise, continuously registered sheet with disciplined type, rules, and signed-off states.
options.viewport: A near-white canvas pairs a large event status plate with a ruled activity ledger and exact operational metadata.
options.case: Exceptional calm and clarity with a distinctive system; it holds product clarity but identifies less immediately with live event work.
options.risk: Can feel like a portfolio rather than a working console if status and controls are too precious.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: A nearly achromatic dashboard carries state in narrow spectral edges.
options.viewport: Soft status bands gather at the edge of a white operational field.
options.case: The calm field is appealing, but the natural-observation metaphor does not identify with event operators or clarify workflow.

options.label: Gravity Garden
options.thesis: Tasks and updates visibly flow toward the events and owners they affect.
options.viewport: Event streams bend toward active workspaces in a spatial field.
options.case: Expressive causality cannot outweigh weak operator recognition and reduced dashboard clarity.
options.kept: Make motion communicate cause and direction.
options.risk: Spatial play competes with fast scanning.

options.label: Glyph Signal
options.thesis: One strict text grid turns operational density into a live signal field.
options.viewport: All metrics, tables, and movement resolve through a single adaptive character grid.
options.case: System discipline is strong, but both audience identification and ordinary administrative clarity suffer.
options.kept: Use a strict density ladder for hierarchy.
options.risk: Accessibility and novelty overwhelm the task.

options.label: Operator Deck
options.thesis: Event control becomes a tactile equipment panel with explicit switches, meters, and modes.
options.viewport: A single equipment fascia exposes every active function and running process.
options.case: Operators recognize the tactility, but the one-fascia topology overloads planning and administration work.
options.kept: Give controls unmistakable resting, armed, and active states.
options.risk: Too many physical metaphors create visual density.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished modern SaaS dashboard with a sidebar, metric cards, charts, tables, and subtle transitions.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar sidebar opens to KPI cards, trend charts, recent activity, and quick actions.
canonCard.risk: Clear and usable, but intentionally indistinguishable from neighboring admin products.
